bull.t: Strong Cash Generation and Balance Sheet
bull.b: Robust cash generation and low leverage provide financial flexibility to fund advanced-fab investment, absorb memory-cycle downturns, and support shareholder returns without relying heavily on external financing.

Long-term customer agreements and substantial minimum commitments can improve demand visibility, strengthen strategic relationships with major buyers, and support capacity planning as Micron expands memory production.

Successful HBM and node transitions position Micron in high-value AI infrastructure and advanced-memory markets, potentially improving product mix and differentiation versus more commoditized memory offerings.

bear.b: Memory pricing and utilization can reverse sharply when supply-demand conditions change, making current exceptional margins and cash flow difficult to sustain and leaving earnings exposed to future downcycles.

Extended industry constraints may limit Micron’s ability to convert demand into shipments, delay capacity expansion, and increase execution risk as the company relies on complex multi-year fab and packaging ramps.

bear.t: High Capital and Operating Expense Requirements
bear.b: Large fab, packaging, technology, and workforce investments raise the fixed-cost base and execution burden, potentially pressuring free cash flow and returns if demand, yields, or pricing weaken during the investment cycle.
